Lessons.Title: The Pythagorean Identity (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Critique (in writing) a strategy using the Pythagorean Identity for identifying the value of sine and tangent from the known value of cosine and the quadrant of the angle. Use the Pythagorean Identity to determine the value of all 3 trigonometric ratios given the value of 1 to start from and the quadrant of the angle.
To recover sin or cos from its square, apply the known quadrant to choose the sign; tanθ=sinθ/cosθ when cosθ!=0.

Source activity 6.1: Math Talk: Which Quadrant?: For an angle \(\theta\) in the quadrant indicated, use mental estimation to identify the values of \(\cos(\theta)\), \(\sin(\theta)\), and \(\tan(\theta)\) as either positive or negative. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 6.2: Andre's Calculations: Suppose that the angle \(\theta\), in radians, is in quadrant 4 of the unit circle. If \(\cos(\theta)=0.28\), what are the values of \(\sin(\theta)\) and \(\tan(\theta)\)? Andre uses the Pythagorean Identity and determines that the value of \(\sin(\theta)\) is -0.96. Using the values of sine and cosine, he then calculates the value of tangent: \(\begin{align}… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 6.3: Card Sort: Where's the Point?: Your teacher will give you a set of cards that should be arranged face up with cards showing values for sine, cosine, and tangent on one side and cards showing quadrants on the other. For each pair, explain to your partner how you know if the pair is or is not possible on the unit circle. Once a pair is identified, place the cards in front of you to use later. For each pair… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: The picture shows angles \(A\) and \(B\). Explain why \(\sin(B) = \text- \sin(A)\) and why \(\cos(B) = \text-\cos(A)\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Which statements are true? Select all that apply. \(\sin(\theta) > 0\) for an angle \(\theta\) in quadrant 2 \(\cos(\theta) > 0\) for an angle \(\theta\) in quadrant 2 \(\tan(\theta) > 0\) for an angle \(\theta\) in quadrant 2 \(\sin(\theta) > 0\) for an angle \(\theta\) in quadrant 3 \(\cos(\theta) > 0\) for an angle… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: The tangent of an angle satisfies \(\tan(\theta) = 10\). Which quadrant could \(\theta\) lie in? Explain how you know. Estimate the possible value(s) of \(\theta\). Explain your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Evaluate each of the following: \(\tan\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\) \(\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\) \(\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: The sine of an angle \(\theta\) in the second quadrant is \(0.6\). What is \(\tan(\theta)\)? Explain how you know. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Triangle \(ABC\) is an isosceles right triangle in the unit circle. Explain why \(\sin(A) = \cos(A)\). Use the Pythagorean Theorem to explain why \(2(\sin(A))^2 = 1\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: Triangle \(DEF\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\). The scale factor going from \(\triangle DEF\) to \(\triangle ABC\) is 3. Explain why the length of segment \(AB\) is 3 times the length of segment \(DE\) and the length of segment \(BC\) is 3 times the length of segment \(EF\). Explain why \(\sin(A) = \sin(D)\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 8: Which of the following is true for angle \(\theta\)? Select all that apply. \(\sin(\theta) < 0\) \(\sin(\theta) > 0\) \(\cos(\theta) < 0\) \(\cos(\theta) > 0\) \(\sin(\theta) > \cos(\theta)\) \(\sin(\theta) < \cos(\theta)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
